reasoning: Classification: Tariff line 32091010 ('Acrylic emulsion (paint)') best matches 'acrylic paint'. Confidence is high.
Preference: Tariff line 32091010 is marked PREFERENTIAL under the India-UAE CEPA.
Tariff: The effective MFN rate is 10% and the 2026 CEPA preferential rate is 0%.
Origin: The product meets rule PSR-IN-R045 ('CTSH + VA 40%') with non-originating inputs outside 320910 and 65.0% value addition.
Saving: Duty savings are estimated at 10000.00 AED based on the 100000.00 AED shipment value.
Procedure: Outlined procedural steps for factory registration, certificate application, issuance, direct consignment, importer claim, and record retention.
Caveats: Included mandatory caveats covering duty scope, CIF valuation, issuer details, and exporter declarations.

origin_result.basis: Final manufacture took place in the UAE. Manufacturing goes beyond minimal operations. CTSH passed as all 2 non-originating inputs are classified outside subheading 320910. Value addition passed at 65.0% against a threshold of 40% on an FOB basis.

procedure.step: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires factory registration outside a free zone prior to certificate application.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: the Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the Certificate of Origin for India e-service for local manufacturers and exporters upon submitting required documents.
the Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for invoice values up to AED 100,000.
the competent authority issues the certificate of origin prior to, at, or within five working days of exportation.
the exporter must ensure direct shipment from the UAE to India and indicate third-party invoicing on the claim if applicable.
the Indian importer claims the preferential tariff treatment when filing the bill of entry and maintains required origin information.
the exporter must retain origin records and cost breakdown details for at least 5 years.

caveats.note: Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
